name: DurableJobCoordinator

enqueue_or_coalesce.transaction: caller-owned LLD-01 UnitOfWork; no nested BEGIN/COMMIT and no Foundation command receipt
steps: resolve exact static job_type + contract_version registration and fail closed when absent
validate payload against the registered packet schema, sensitivity policy and Foundation canonical JSON bounds before persistence
require caller dedupe_key to be a bounded non-empty UTF-8 string and require the registered packet coalescing contract to derive the exact same semantic key from the validated payload
compute dedupe_sha256 as lowercase SHA-256 of strict canonical JSON {schema:'SOMA_DURABLE_JOB_DEDUPE_V1',job_type,contract_version,dedupe_key}; raw dedupe_key is not persisted by Foundation
using idx_jobs_dedupe_state load at most two rows for exact job_type + contract_version + dedupe_sha256 whose state is in the registered coalesce_states

for every candidate validate canonical persisted payload against the exact registered contract and re-derive the semantic dedupe key; hash collision, payload/key disagreement, unsupported contract or more than one matching row fails INTEGRITY_FAILURE rather than guessing
if exactly one valid matching row exists return its job_id without mutation
otherwise INSERT one queued durable_jobs row with canonical payload_json, dedupe_sha256, attempt_count=0, null checkpoint/claim/error and server timestamps; plain INSERT only
enqueue_or_coalesce.concurrency: BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialization plus uq_jobs_active_dedupe guarantees at most one active queued/running/waiting_review/retry_wait job for one job_type + contract_version + semantic dedupe identity; contract-specific coalescing may additionally include completed and is checked through the indexed exact lookup
enqueue_or_coalesce.legacy: pre-migration-8 rows with dedupe_sha256=NULL are never silently treated as a coalescing match or backfilled from payload by Foundation

claim.precondition: host owns canonical data instance and is READY or explicitly allowed background-start state
claim.selection: select due queued/retry_wait job by deterministic ordering (next_attempt_at_utc NULL/earliest, created_at_utc, job_id)
guards: job_type + contract_version is present in the static registry before claim
payload_json is exact canonical registered payload and dedupe_sha256 is non-null/valid for post-migration-8 jobs
retry_wait is claimable only when next_attempt_at_utc <= now; queued with NULL next_attempt_at_utc is immediately due
claim.mutation: set state=running, claimed_run_id=current run_id, claim_started_at_utc=now, attempt_count=attempt_count+1, updated_at_utc=now
claim.claim_token: JobClaim binds job_id, job_type, contract_version, run_id, attempt_ordinal=post-increment attempt_count and claim_started_at_utc; later handler writes must match the complete tuple so a stale handler in the same process cannot act on a newer attempt
claim.unknown_contract: unknown/unsupported due job is never executed; coordinator fails it safe with bounded technical error evidence or returns an integrity-safe diagnostic disposition according to the static registry policy, then later claim calls may progress
claim.commit: commit claim before external/file work begins

execute: run job-specific handler outside authoritative write transaction in background executor; handler may persist bounded checkpoints using short explicit transactions and must invoke owning-domain commands for accepted domain mutations

steps: reload exact job
verify state=running and exact job_id/run_id/attempt_ordinal/claim_started_at_utc claim tuple
validate checkpoint against exact registered checkpoint schema and Foundation canonical JSON bounds
write canonical checkpoint_json and updated_at_utc only
COMMIT
checkpoint.stale_claim: any tuple mismatch returns JOB_CLAIM_CONFLICT and changes nothing

steps: reload exact job and verify state=running plus complete exact claim tuple
verify job_attempts has no row for this job_id + attempt_ordinal
insert one job_attempts terminal row with ordinal=attempt_ordinal, run_id from exact claim, started_at_utc=claim_started_at_utc, finished_at_utc=server-now and outcome=completed
set durable_jobs state=completed, clear claim fields and next_attempt_at_utc, update technical checkpoint state only as contract permits, set updated_at_utc=server-now
COMMIT
complete.stale_claim: any tuple mismatch or duplicate attempt ordinal fails closed and never rewrites the newer attempt

steps: verify complete exact current claim tuple
validate bounded stable error_code; raw exception/secret/path/provider content is forbidden
insert exactly one job_attempts row outcome=failed for the exact current attempt ordinal
job-type retry policy classifies terminal failed vs retry_wait with explicit next_attempt_at_utc
clear claim fields, store bounded last_error_code and update updated_at_utc
COMMIT
fail_or_retry.rule: retry schedule is technical workflow policy; it never fabricates domain lifecycle state
fail_or_retry.stale_claim: any tuple mismatch returns JOB_CLAIM_CONFLICT with no state/attempt mutation

cancel.transaction: caller-owned UnitOfWork; no nested BEGIN/COMMIT and no Foundation command receipt
cancel.input: job_id + exact expected job_type/contract_version + owning-domain command_context
steps: load the exact durable_jobs row inside the caller UnitOfWork and require job_type/contract_version equal the caller expectation; mismatch or missing identity fails closed
if state=cancelled return ALREADY_CANCELLED without mutation
if state=completed or failed return TERMINAL_UNCHANGED without rewriting technical history

if state=running capture claimed_run_id, claim_started_at_utc and attempt_count, require that job_attempts lacks that exact ordinal, insert exactly one job_attempts row outcome=cancelled for that current ordinal, then set durable_jobs state=cancelled and clear claimed_run_id/claim_started_at_utc/next_attempt_at_utc
if state=queued, retry_wait or waiting_review set durable_jobs state=cancelled and clear next_attempt_at_utc/claim fields without inventing a job_attempts row for work that never held a running claim
set updated_at_utc=server-now and return DurableJobCancellationResultV1 to the owning-domain caller; caller decides whether to commit or roll the entire shared UnitOfWork back
rules: a revoked running handler loses coordinator authority immediately at commit; checkpoint/complete/fail must revalidate the complete exact claim tuple and reject the stale worker
an already-running handler may physically finish in-flight external CPU/file work, but that work cannot regain coordinator or owning-domain authority merely because it finishes
an optional in-process cancellation signal may be delivered only after commit as a latency optimization; correctness depends on persisted state/claim validation, never on that signal
the same owning-domain rollback that rejects cancellation also restores the prior durable job state/job-attempt history atomically

startup_recovery.precondition: new host already owns canonical data instance exclusively
steps: find state=running jobs whose claimed_run_id differs from current run in deterministic job_id order
for each stale row use its own short BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and revalidate the exact stale claim tuple before mutation
validate exact job contract/version; unknown contract fails safe and never executes
insert job_attempts outcome=interrupted using stored claim_started_at_utc, stale claimed_run_id and attempt_count ordinal only when that ordinal has not already been represented
apply exact registered job-type crash recovery policy: queued, retry_wait, failed, or waiting_review
clear stale claim fields and persist bounded stable technical error/disposition
never resume arbitrary in-memory code position; restart only from durable checkpoint/contract
startup_recovery.concurrency: revalidation under the writer transaction makes recovery idempotent; a row already recovered or otherwise changed is skipped/handled from current persisted state rather than receiving duplicate attempt history

restore_reconciliation.precondition: a cryptographically and structurally verified historical database has replaced the live database, host remains QUIESCING, restored DB is open through the verified LLD-12 SQLCipher provider, and no coordinator claims are permitted yet
restore_reconciliation.transaction: one LLD-01 recovery-finalization UnitOfWork before runtime may become READY
steps: enumerate all restored durable_jobs in deterministic job_id order whose state is queued, running, waiting_review, or retry_wait

for a restored running row with a valid prior claimed_run_id/claim_started_at_utc, insert exactly one job_attempts row outcome=interrupted using that prior run identity and attempt_count ordinal if that ordinal is not already represented

set every restored nonterminal durable_jobs row to cancelled, clear claimed_run_id/claim_started_at_utc/next_attempt_at_utc, set last_error_code=RESTORE_SNAPSHOT_JOB_INVALIDATED, and preserve bounded payload/checkpoint/dedupe identity only as historical technical evidence
leave completed, failed, and already-cancelled rows unchanged
commit this reconciliation in the same recovery-finalization boundary that records required restore receipt/audit evidence, before enabling ordinary job claims
rules: restoring a historical snapshot never silently replays queued/retry/waiting external work
no job-type opt-in restore-resume exists in Beta 1.0; an operator or owning-domain workflow must explicitly start genuinely desired new work after readiness
restored job cancellation is technical workflow reconciliation and does not reverse or fabricate owning-domain lifecycle state
unknown job type/version remains fail-closed and cannot become executable during restore

job_type_contract.registration: static application registry; unknown persisted job type/version is quarantined/failed-safe and not guessed
job_type_contract.rule: Foundation may hash/compare a packet semantic dedupe key but never invents its meaning; the owning packet contract deterministically derives the exact key from validated payload and declares which technical states are coalescing matches

concurrency: one coordinator in one authoritative host; at most two background executor workers; migration-8 indexed semantic coalescing plus the packet contract provides stronger per-source/per-type identity without unbounded payload scans
shutdown: QUIESCING stops new claims; running handlers receive cooperative cancellation signal and either finish a safe checkpoint/terminal result or remain recoverable as prior-run interruption after process exit
